title: TUF root and role policy, and trusted client state, v1
description: The two halves SR-014 records as missing: the role policy the release authority publishes, and the trusted state a client holds. docs/operations/RELEASE_VERIFICATION.md and ADR-013 are the normative owners; packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql#tuf_roots holds the root and #tuf_metadata holds the client state. TUF's security properties are client-side, so the record that matters is the client's own view: a client refuses metadata that is older than what it trusts, expired, or signed below threshold, and each of those three refusals is a named attack rather than an error condition. D-024 makes hostile-metadata tests a release requirement and nothing here is evidence that any has been run.

roles.description: One entry per TUF role. Thresholds and expiry windows differ per role because the roles defend different attacks: a short timestamp window is the freeze-attack control and a high root threshold is the key-compromise control, and giving them one number would make each wrong.

threshold.description: The minimum number of distinct signatures. D-091 records that the project has one maintainer, so a root threshold above one is unsatisfiable today and the operations contract records that as a weakness rather than describing the checklist substitute as equivalent.

expiry_policy_key.description: A key in packages/schemas/policy-defaults-v1.json. D-239 fixes the cadences: timestamp 1 day, snapshot 7 days, targets 90 days, root 365 days re-signed at 270.

online_key.description: True for a key the signing service holds, which is timestamp and snapshot. Root and targets keys are offline; an online root key removes the property the role exists to provide.

trusted_state.description: What one client trusts for one role right now. It is per device rather than per account because the trust decision belongs to the installation that will run the binary.

version.description: Monotonic. Metadata at or below this version is refused, which is the rollback-attack control. The previous version and digest are retained so the refusal is recordable rather than merely correct.

expires_at.description: Past this, the client stops trusting the repository rather than continuing on stale metadata. That is the freeze-attack control, and it is why an offline client eventually refuses to update rather than quietly staying where it is.

last_refusal_reason_code.description: The refusal is recorded rather than discarded, because a rollback or freeze attempt is a security event and a client that only refuses it leaves no evidence that it happened. The field is unpopulated today and that is stated rather than hidden: packages/schemas/reason-codes-v1.json has three transports — problem, claim-rejection and appraisal — and a local client-side refusal reaches none of them, so no code for one is registered and registering one under a transport it does not use would be worse than leaving it absent.
